teaches: an ordinary final consonant carrying fathatan is spelled with the unpronounced support alif
the tied taa is one of the three exempt graphemes; the support alif is blocked outright
the variant final a-spelling is a second exempt grapheme; fathatan sits directly on it
a hamza already seated on an alif carrier is the third exempt grapheme; no second alif is added
the article and nunation together are a written contradiction (nun-r4); the table refuses outright rather than repairing a guess about which marker wins
the support-alif question only ever arises for the a-form; a u-form construction is out of this table's regime and is never licensed by analogy
a bare hamza that is not seated on alif does not qualify for the hamza exemption (nun-r3); overgeneralizing 'hamza-final means exempt' is refused and the ordinary support-alif outcome still applies
with no declared tanwin mark there is no evidence to decide the support-alif question from at all
no declared construction at all leaves nothing to license

transfer: the exact-seat requirement behind nun-r2/nun-r3 extends to any other untabulated hamza seat, not only the bare-hamza case already drilled in nun-adv-03 -- resemblance to the licensed alif-seat row never substitutes for a matching construction key
